answer: Preference for one people or faith is common. Pew counted 43 countries with an official religion and 40 more that favour one, including Denmark and the United Kingdom; Greece's constitution names Orthodoxy the prevailing religion. Germany, Greece, Ireland and Armenia give citizenship by descent or ethnic tie; Israel's Law of Return does so for Jews and their relatives, and the Palestinian Basic Law names Islam the official religion. Israel's Declaration of Independence promises complete equality; the 2018 Nation-State law says self-determination is unique to the Jewish people and does not mention equality. Scholars call Israel an ethnic democracy, an ethnocracy or a democracy, and many stress that it also rules millions of non-citizens in the West Bank. The United States limited naturalisation to free white persons in 1790, set national-origins quotas in 1924, and ended them in 1965.

facts.text: Two models dominate the scholarly debate: Sammy Smooha classes Israel as an 'ethnic democracy' (contrary to its self-image as a Western liberal democracy, the Jews appropriate the state, yet Israel extends rights to its Arab citizens), and Oren Yiftachel as an 'ethnocracy' that promotes the expansion of the dominant group in contested territory while keeping a democratic facade.

sources.title: The model of ethnic democracy: Israel as a Jewish and democratic state
sources.quote: Contrary to its self-image and international reputation as a Western liberal democracy, Israel is an ethnic democracy

sources.title: Democracy in Israel/Palestine Today
sources.quote: The first model for defining Israeli democracy is proffered by Sam Smooha and Ruth Gavison's notion of "ethnic democracy,"

sources.title: Democracy in Israel/Palestine Today
sources.quote: Ethnocratic regimes promote the expansion of the dominant group in contested territory and its domination of power structures while maintaining a democratic façade

contested: How to classify Israel. Sammy Smooha: an 'ethnic democracy'. Oren Yiftachel: an 'ethnocracy' that keeps a democratic facade. Others, including many Israeli scholars Yiftachel lists, call it a liberal or constitutional democracy, and indices such as Freedom House and V-Dem classify Israel inside the Green Line as a democracy with flaws. Critics who say that a state defined as Jewish is racist (Warshawsky) or that it must be a theocracy or an apartheid state (Nusseibeh) argue from the definition; defenders point to equal citizenship in law and to the Supreme Court's 2021 ruling. The card reports who uses the word and why; it does not use it as its own description of any country.

The objection that Israel's case differs from Germany's or Greece's because Israel also rules millions of Palestinians in the West Bank who are not citizens and cannot vote in its elections; Freedom House rates the West Bank separately at 22 of 100. Defenders reply that the territory's status is disputed and tied to the conflict, and that citizens inside the Green Line have equal rights in law.

Whether the Law of Return is comparable to Germany's Article 116, Greece's homogeneis or Armenia's rules. Those provide citizenship by descent or ethnic tie, as does Israel's law, but differ in scope, history (Germany's was tied to postwar expulsions) and in whether the favoured group is also the dominant one in the state. How far each is 'the same' is a judgement, not a measurement.

Whether America was 'open' from the start. The 1790 law admitted only free white persons to citizenship, yet before 1882 federal law set almost no numerical limits; historians weigh these differently. The 1965 Act is the end of national-origins quotas, not of all restriction (it added the first numerical cap on the Western Hemisphere).
Freedom House and V-Dem are independent, but each makes judgement calls; the two disagree on some rankings (for example Greece against Israel).

not_claimed: That preferring one people or religion is harmless: it can disadvantage minorities, and several of these states have been criticised for it.
That other countries' practices make any specific Israeli law just, or any other country's law just.
That Israel is, or is not, a democracy in every respect; the card gives indices and the scholarly disagreement.
That the United States has never been, or is now, closed to immigration; it states what the laws said when.
